Policy / Rule (current): Actor must be admin or hold HR_admin. On update: nobody edits their own account; an HR_admin worker may not edit a fellow manager (admin or HR_admin). Only an admin may grant HR_admin. Role is forced to worker.
Description (why the rule is this): features.md 'HR_admin gates worker/user management'. Self-edit is blocked so a manager cannot lock themselves out or self-escalate; HR_admin cannot mint another HR_admin (escalation closed 2026-07-04). Forcing role=worker means editing an admin here would demote them — flagged, not a permission rule.

Policy / Rule (current): Actor admin or HR_admin; not self; HR_admin may not target a fellow manager.
Description (why the rule is this): Same manager hierarchy as upsert_worker so activation cannot be used to bypass the edit rule.

Policy / Rule (current): Actor admin or HR_admin; not self; HR_admin may not target a fellow manager.
Description (why the rule is this): Same hierarchy; deleting self would orphan the session, deleting a peer manager would let HR_admin remove admins.

Policy / Rule (current): No in-app actor. Platform-level: caller (Django admin site / ops script) authorizes.
Description (why the rule is this): features.md 'Company suspension is a platform-level operation'; a company admin must not be able to suspend or resurrect their own tenant.

Policy / Rule (current): Company scoping only; any authenticated member sees the whole user list.
Description (why the rule is this): User's decision 2026-07-04: 'users list stays open to all workers' — needed for people pickers (assigned worker, monitors, related person).

Policy / Rule (current): Admin: every company request. Worker: own submissions OR any request whose target type they hold the matching modify permission for (PERMISSION_BY_TARGET).
Description (why the rule is this): Widened 2026-07-14: a permission holder can make the change directly anyway, so seeing others' proposals leaks nothing; requester sees own to follow status.

Policy / Rule (current): Admin, or holder of the target type's modify permission. The requester gets no review power from having submitted.
Description (why the rule is this): Reviewer = anyone who could have written directly; otherwise a worker could approve their own request.

Policy / Rule (current): Requester OR can_review_request; another company's id is not_found, same company but unrelated is forbidden.
Description (why the rule is this): Per-row twin of the list rule so list and detail cannot disagree; not_found outside the tenant reveals nothing.

Policy / Rule (current): can_review_request; request resolved within company; already-reviewed → conflict.
Description (why the rule is this): Approval writes to the real model, so it must carry the same permission as a direct write.

Policy / Rule (current): No check; display helper.
Proposed policy call: none — caller must obtain the request via get_user_request
Description (why the rule is this): Pure formatting; the only callers already loaded the request through the gated lookup.

Policy / Rule (current): No check; locks the row and refuses non-pending. Trusts the caller.
Proposed policy call: none — internal; only review_user_request may call
Description (why the rule is this): Authorization belongs to the service; the model only guarantees atomic once-only application.

Policy / Rule (current): A securing request applies only if the requester still actively holds the customer at approval time.
Description (why the rule is this): features.md pool rule 2: approving a stale hold would hand a customer to a worker who no longer has a claim on it.

Policy / Rule (current): Delegates to policy.has_perm / policy.has_company_perm (admin implicit for user codes; nobody implicit for company codes).
Description (why the rule is this): Single reader of role + JSON lists; every legacy call site keeps working.

Policy / Rule (current): Target type → modify permission (color/product/customer).
Description (why the rule is this): Only requestable codes may have a request target; the catalog test asserts the two tables agree.

Policy / Rule (current): Admin or view_all_customers → all company customers; else assigned OR monitored OR in a pool whose access list includes the user (distinct).
Description (why the rule is this): features.md 'view_all_customers gates customer visibility'; workers only work customers assigned to/monitored by them; pool access grants read visibility.

Policy / Rule (current): A follow-up is visible iff its customer is (same clause as get_filtered_customers).
Proposed policy call: object policy for CustomerFollowUp (visible via customer)
Description (why the rule is this): Follow-ups carry customer contact history; visibility must never exceed the customer's.

Policy / Rule (current): Per-row twin of get_filtered_customers (company check, view_all, assigned, monitor, pool access).
Description (why the rule is this): One rule for list and detail; currently duplicated inline in customers/views.view_customer — the object policy removes that copy.

Policy / Rule (current): Direct: admin, assigned worker, a monitor, or a modify_followup holder who can view the customer. Pool member on an unheld pool customer: allowed and starts a hold; member who already holds it: allowed and extends the hold. Anyone else (incl. member while another holds it): forbidden. Never requestable.
Proposed policy call: policy.is_admin / policy.has_perm(MODIFY_FOLLOWUP) + policy.can_view; hold logic stays in service
Description (why the rule is this): User's decision 2026-07-05: one follow-up rule everywhere. Follow-ups are the everyday way holds begin (features.md 'Follow-ups'); the customer row is locked so two members can't both become holder.

Policy / Rule (current): Admin only; no permission code; never requestable.
Description (why the rule is this): features.md 'Deleting a follow-up is admin-only'; deleting history is destructive and unexposed in UI/API.

Policy / Rule (current): modify_customer → direct write (may assign, set pool, debt). Without it → UserRequest: creating is open to any worker; updating requires target.assigned_worker == caller; assigned_worker_id rides on the request (validated now and at approval); debt/pool/monitors never ride on a request.
Proposed policy call: policy.write_mode(MODIFY_CUSTOMER) + assigned-worker check on REQUEST path
Description (why the rule is this): SECURITY FIX 2026-07-04: previously any worker could queue an update for any customer (visibility bypass). Request-edit boundary = assigned worker, a subset of read visibility.

Policy / Rule (current): modify_customer; not requestable (forbidden without it).
Description (why the rule is this): api.md: customer deletes are 'not requestable' — destructive, and the row carries debt/history.

Policy / Rule (current): modify_customer; no UserRequest fallback.
Description (why the rule is this): features.md: pool management (rule knobs, access list) is modify_customer-gated; pools decide who can claim customers so they must not be requestable.

Policy / Rule (current): modify_customer; not requestable.
Description (why the rule is this): Same as upsert_pool; deleting releases member customers to 'no pool'.

Policy / Rule (current): Caller must be on the pool's access list (CustomerPool.workers); customer must be in a pool and not actively held by anyone else. No admin/permission bypass.
Proposed policy call: keep as object-level rule in service (pool membership)
Description (why the rule is this): features.md 'Holding': a claim is a worker's personal action; an admin bypass would let admins hold on behalf of nobody. Company-scoped lookup (not_found across tenants).

Policy / Rule (current): Only the current active holder may secure; no admin/permission bypass. Pool auth_rule 2 → records an update UserRequest (assigned_worker_id + secure_hold) instead of writing.
Proposed policy call: keep as object-level rule in service; REQUEST branch driven by pool.auth_rule
Description (why the rule is this): features.md 'Securing': ownership is earned by the holder; rule 2 (成交后需管理员审核) defers to an admin/modify_customer reviewer.

Policy / Rule (current): modify_customer; forbidden otherwise (no request).
Description (why the rule is this): A bulk update that overwrites debt and fields; the same code as direct customer writes.

Policy / Rule (current): Company scoping only; every member sees all suppliers.
Proposed policy call: none (tenant scope) — candidate: company entitlement inventory_software
Description (why the rule is this): Docstring: 'modify_supplier gates writes only'. Supplier data is catalog-like; open read matches products/colors. Belongs to the 经销存 feature group.

Policy / Rule (current): modify_supplier; forbidden otherwise; no request fallback.
Description (why the rule is this): Added with the purchasing family; suppliers feed purchasing documents, so writes are restricted, and there is no approval workflow for them.

Policy / Rule (current): Company scoping only; any authenticated member reads the whole catalog.
Description (why the rule is this): api.md: 'whole company catalog readable by ANY authenticated company user (permissions gate writes only, same as web)'. Every worker needs the catalog to fill customer/order forms.

Policy / Rule (current): modify_color → direct; else records a create/update UserRequest (pending image stored on the request).
Description (why the rule is this): Approach A (2026-07): permission holder writes directly, others propose; catalog edits are low-risk enough to be requestable.

Policy / Rule (current): modify_color → delete; else records a delete UserRequest with a name/custom_id snapshot.
Description (why the rule is this): Color deletes became requestable (was 403) so workers can propose clean-up; snapshot keeps the request readable after deletion.

Policy / Rule (current): modify_color; forbidden otherwise; NOT requestable.
Description (why the rule is this): Archive is an idempotent flag flip with no approval path — a deliberate exception to the color REQUEST mode. Consider making archive requestable or documenting the exception.

Policy / Rule (current): modify_product → direct (incl. parent move, dynamic fields); else UserRequest.
Description (why the rule is this): Same approach A as colors; parent/cycle validation re-runs at approval time.

Policy / Rule (current): modify_product → delete (children re-parented by signal); else delete UserRequest.
Description (why the rule is this): Product DELETE became requestable (was 403).

Policy / Rule (current): modify_product; forbidden otherwise; not requestable.
Description (why the rule is this): Same exception as archive_color.

Policy / Rule (current): Were modify_color / modify_product; currently disabled.
Description (why the rule is this): Excel imports are bulk direct writes; same code as the direct write path.

Policy / Rule (current): Company scoping only; every member sees all warehouses and stock.
Proposed policy call: none (tenant scope) — candidate: company entitlement inventory_software
Description (why the rule is this): Docstring: 'modify_warehouse gates writes only'. Stock quantities are operational data every order handler needs; belongs to 经销存.

Policy / Rule (current): modify_warehouse; forbidden otherwise; no request fallback.
Description (why the rule is this): Warehouses are configuration rows referenced by stock and orders; no approval workflow exists for them.

Policy / Rule (current): INTERNAL primitive: no permission check; locks the row; negative allowed.
Proposed policy call: none — must only be called by adjust_stock or order posting services
Description (why the rule is this): Docstring: 'intended to be called by order processing'. The permission belongs to the calling operation (adjust vs. receipt posting), not the primitive.

Policy / Rule (current): modify_stock; forbidden otherwise.
Description (why the rule is this): A manual, user-driven quantity change is a privileged correction; order-driven movements will carry modify_purchase (etc.) instead.

Policy / Rule (current): Company scoping only; every member sees all accounts incl. balance.
Proposed policy call: candidate: policy.require(a view code) or company entitlement inventory_software
Description (why the rule is this): Docstring says 'modify_bank_account gates writes only', but balances and balance_history are sensitive. Unlike customers there is no view_* code. Decision pending (open item from the design review).

Policy / Rule (current): modify_bank_account; forbidden otherwise. balance/balance_history never writable here (not even admins).
Description (why the rule is this): Money movements must go through record_payment so the history stays an audit trail.

Policy / Rule (current): modify_bank_account; forbidden otherwise.
Description (why the rule is this): Moves money and appends to the ledger; same code as account writes (no separate 'pay' code yet).

Policy / Rule (current): Company scoping only; every member sees every order of every kind.
Proposed policy call: object policy for Order (visible) — rule TBD (todo_new.txt)
Description (why the rule is this): Docstring TODO(visibility). Purchase documents carry supplier prices; likely rule: admin / modify_purchase holders see all purchasing docs, others none or own (created_by). Decision pending.

Policy / Rule (current): Company scoping only; not_found for another tenant's id.
Proposed policy call: object policy for Order (can_view) — must mirror get_filtered_orders
Description (why the rule is this): todo_new.txt: the detail must apply the same rule as the list; return forbidden for a company row the profile may not open.

Policy / Rule (current): modify_purchase; forbidden before anything is read or written; no request fallback.
Description (why the rule is this): Module docstring: public save_* entry points own the gate; purchasing documents post to stock and money, so no approval fallback.

Policy / Rule (current): No permission check by design; trusts the caller; company-scoped references only.
Proposed policy call: none — never call from a view; a grep test should enforce
Description (why the rule is this): Module docstring: 'must never be called from an API view or a web view directly'.

Policy / Rule (current): Customers: candidates come from get_filtered_customers (visibility applies). Products/colors/pools/users: company-wide.
Proposed policy call: inherits object policies (Customer visible) — extend when Order gets one
Description (why the rule is this): Search must never surface a row the list wouldn't; it reuses the customer visibility service. Other types are company-open today, matching their list services.

Policy / Rule (current): Every API view requires a valid JWT except login/logout.
Description (why the rule is this): Authentication is a different question from authorization; services assume an authenticated profile.

Policy / Rule (current): Authenticated user without a UserProfile → 403.
Description (why the rule is this): A User row with no profile has no company; it cannot be scoped, so refuse. Six identical copies should collapse into one base view.

Policy / Rule (current): DRF permission classes mirroring the service rules.
Description (why the rule is this): No view uses them (only AllowAny appears in views). Docs still advertise them. Under the service-only rule they would duplicate the gate.

Policy / Rule (current): Filter a viewset queryset to the request's company.
Description (why the rule is this): No viewsets exist; services already scope every query.

Function / Site: UserListView / WorkerUpsertView / WorkerActivateView / WorkerDeactivateView / WorkerDeleteView / UserRequestListView / UserRequestApproveView / UserRequestRejectView
Policy / Rule (current): No check in the view; inherits the service rule (manager hierarchy / review rule).
Description (why the rule is this): Module docstring: 'The views only require an authenticated user with a profile; the service does the real authorization.'

Policy / Rule (current): Loads via get_user_request; ALSO computes can_review for the client (ask-only).
Proposed policy call: policy predicate for the flag; service for access
Description (why the rule is this): The flag tells the mobile app whether to draw 通过/拒绝; the actual review is re-checked server-side.

Policy / Rule (current): No check in the view; inherits service rule. Upsert returns 202 pending_approval when the service recorded a request.
Description (why the rule is this): api.md: thin adapters; the 202 branch is the REQUEST write mode surfacing to the client.

Function / Site: ColorListUpsertView / ColorDeleteView / ColorArchiveView / ProductListUpsertView / ProductDeleteView / ProductArchiveView
Policy / Rule (current): No check in the view; inherits service rule (REQUEST for upsert/delete, forbid for archive).
Description (why the rule is this): Same pattern; note archive returns 403 while delete returns 202 for the same worker — the catalog-level exception noted above.

Policy / Rule (current): No check in the view; inherits service rule.
Description (why the rule is this): Same pattern.

Policy / Rule (current): No check in the view; inherits service rule. GET is open to every member.
Description (why the rule is this): See get_filtered_bank_accounts.

Policy / Rule (current): No check in the view; reads inherit the (missing) visibility rule; POST inherits modify_purchase.
Description (why the rule is this): Module docstring: 'Reads are open to every authenticated company user for now: per-user visibility is pending.'

Policy / Rule (current): No check; inherits search service scoping.
Description (why the rule is this): Same pattern.

Policy / Rule (current): Session-authenticated user required; redirects to login.
Description (why the rule is this): Web equivalent of IsAuthenticated.

Policy / Rule (current): Profile role must be admin; workers are redirected to worker_dashboard with a flash.
Description (why the rule is this): Admin dashboard is the admin's workspace (approvals, employees, config). Page-level convenience only; every POST action inside still goes through a gated service.

Policy / Rule (current): Admin or HR_admin holder; others redirected.
Description (why the rule is this): The worker-edit page is meaningless to non-managers; the service re-checks the finer hierarchy (self / peer manager) on save.

Policy / Rule (current): After login: admin → admin_dashboard, worker → worker_dashboard, other → error.
Description (why the rule is this): Pure navigation; kept out of the policy but should stop comparing the role literal.

Policy / Rule (current): Pick the dashboard by role.
Description (why the rule is this): Three copies of the same role literal; navigation only.

Policy / Rule (current): Page: admin_required. Actions: worker/customer/pool/request actions delegate to services; visit_worker stores the target worker id in the session; reminders via _process_reminder_actions.
Description (why the rule is this): Every write on the page is a service call; the page gate just keeps workers off a screen full of admin controls.

Policy / Rule (current): Worker: sees their own workspace. Admin: must have session['visiting_worker_profile_id'] set (read-only visit); otherwise redirected. In visiting mode every management action is refused ('查看模式下无法执行此操作'). Section/button flags come from the VIEWED profile's permissions (can_modify_*, is_hr_admin, view_all_customers). HR section only with HR_admin.
Proposed policy call: page: login; flags: policy.has_perm(viewed_profile, …) (ask-only); visiting guard stays in view
Description (why the rule is this): features.md 'visit worker': an admin views a worker's dashboard read-only. Flags are UI hints; the services authorize the real logged-in user, which is why acting in visiting mode is blocked in the view (the admin would otherwise act with their own admin rights on the worker's page).

Policy / Rule (current): manager_required; the HR_admin checkbox is disabled unless the actor is admin.
Description (why the rule is this): Mirrors ensure_can_grant so the form can't even offer what the service will refuse.

Policy / Rule (current): POST only; delegates to review_user_request.
Description (why the rule is this): Thin adapter.

Policy / Rule (current): Delete: only the reminder's owner (filter owner=request.user, company). Create: owner = request.user; linked customer must be in accessible_customers (the caller's visible set); related person must be an active user of the company.
Proposed policy call: move into a users service (upsert_reminder / delete_reminder) using policy.visible(Customer)
Status: enforced in the VIEW (violates service-only rule)
Description (why the rule is this): Reminders are personal to-dos (features.md 'Reminder … belongs to one owner'); the customer link must respect customer visibility. Logic currently lives in the view and writes Reminder rows directly — needs a service.

Policy / Rule (current): Inline: admin OR assigned OR monitor OR pool access OR view_all_customers, else 403. Request mode (?request_id=) bypasses this and uses get_user_request + can_review_request.
Description (why the rule is this): Re-implements the service rule line by line; the object policy makes this one call. Request mode bypass is correct: a reviewer needs to see the target even if they can't normally view it.

Policy / Rule (current): writes_directly = modify_customer. can_edit_info = new customer OR writes_directly OR assigned worker. can_modify_followup = can_modify_followups(). Assignment/debt/pool fields posted only when the user may set them; 'save_customer_info' refused without can_edit_info.
Proposed policy call: policy.write_mode(MODIFY_CUSTOMER) + policy predicates (ask-only); the service still enforces
Description (why the rule is this): Form gating mirrors upsert_customer so a worker never sees fields the request path would drop; the service is the real gate.

Policy / Rule (current): Inline: modify_customer else 403.
Description (why the rule is this): Page-level copy of upsert_pool's rule; fine as a page gate but should use the shared decorator rather than an inline literal.

Policy / Rule (current): No view check; service gate (modify_customer).
Description (why the rule is this): Thin adapter.

Policy / Rule (current): Inline: role must be admin else 403; then writes Company.import_structure directly in the view.
Proposed policy call: policy.require_admin inside a NEW users service (update_import_mapping); page: admin_only
Status: enforced in the VIEW (violates service-only rule; no service exists)
Description (why the rule is this): Company configuration is admin-only (no code grants it). The write bypasses the service layer entirely — must move into a service so the API could reuse it and the grep test passes.

Policy / Rule (current): can_modify = modify_color / modify_product (button label 修改 vs 申请修改); writes delegate to the service which decides direct vs request.
Description (why the rule is this): UI hint only; the service returns .pending when it recorded a request.

Policy / Rule (current): get_user_request (requester / reviewer) + can_review_request for the buttons; wrong target type → redirect to the right detail page.
Proposed policy call: object policy for UserRequest (can_view) + policy predicate
Description (why the rule is this): Same as the customer request mode.

Policy / Rule (current): Were: admin-only for structure/mapping config; service-gated for imports.
Proposed policy call: policy.require_admin in a config service when re-enabled
Description (why the rule is this): Same company-config rule as customer_import_mapping.

Policy / Rule (current): login only; service scopes results.
Description (why the rule is this): Thin adapter.

Policy / Rule (current): Declared; never checked anywhere in live code.
Proposed policy call: policy.require_company_perm at the group level: inventory_software → suppliers / purchasing / warehouses / stock / finance services; crm_software → customers / follow-ups / pools; AI_assistant / platform_integration → their features when built
Description (why the rule is this): Feature entitlements per tenant (features.md). Natural wiring is one require_company_perm per service group so a company without 经销存 cannot reach purchasing even with user codes. Whether to wire or drop is an open decision.
